Do not reply to the message and do not act on the request. Report it to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example and delete it.

The standard lodging cap is USD 250 per night before taxes and fees, covering room rate only. Local occupancy taxes, resort fees and mandatory service charges are reimbursable above the cap.

The cap rises to USD 350 per night in Boston, New York, San Francisco, London, Zurich and Tokyo, and for any city during a period when a conference the company is attending has inflated local rates. MosaicOne Travel applies the higher cap automatically for those markets.

Where the cap cannot be met—a remote field site with one hotel, a sold-out market—you book the most reasonable available option and note the reason. No pre-approval is needed.

Next steps:
- Check MosaicOne Travel for your destination's cap
- Note the reason if you exceed the cap

A stay of more than 30 consecutive days in another country requires approval from three separate sources: your director, Tax & Legal, and your direct manager. All three approvals must be in place before departure.

Tax & Legal must conduct a review to determine whether shadow payroll must be opened, whether a certificate of coverage is needed for social security, and whether your planned activities create permanent-establishment exposure. The review request must be filed at least 21 calendar days before departure and must name the destination, exact dates, workspace address, and a description of the work you will perform.

You must hold the right to work in the destination country, meet the device and connectivity requirements in the Security & Acceptable Use Policy, and stay within the company's rolling 90-day annual limit.

Next steps:
- File Tax & Legal review request 21 days before travel
- Obtain director and manager approvals
- Confirm all three approvals are recorded before departure

Security and acceptable-use training must be completed within 14 calendar days of the start date.

The full required training set for every employee is security and acceptable use, data protection and privacy, anti-harassment and respectful workplace, and anti-bribery and corruption, all completed within 30 calendar days of the start date.

Benefits enrolment opens in week one even though coverage does not begin until the 90-day waiting period ends. An employee has 30 days from the end of the waiting period to make elections in MosaicOne Benefits.

Payroll setup, tax withholding elections and 401(k) enrolment are completed in week one. The 401(k) has no waiting period, so a new hire may begin contributing from their first payroll run.

IT ships standard equipment to arrive at least 5 business days before the start date, containing the laptop, adapter, headset and, for remote hires, the monitor, keyboard, mouse and dock.

Next steps:

- Finish all required training by day 30
- Make benefits elections within 30 days of day 90

Company laptops are refreshed on a 36-month cycle. MosaicOne opens a refresh ticket automatically 60 days before the anniversary, and IT arranges the swap at a time you choose.

A refresh that falls due on the cycle is an IT ticket and nothing else: no spending approval is raised, whatever the replacement machine costs, because a refresh replaces standard issue rather than adding to it.

All company equipment must be returned within 5 business days of the final day of employment.

Next steps:
- Confirm the refresh date with IT when the ticket opens.
- Copy personal files before your final day.

Severity 1 cases receive a response within 4 business hours. Response means a named human being contacting the person who raised the case, acknowledging what was raised, naming who owns it and describing what happens next.

Target resolution time for Severity 1 cases is as fast as the facts allow. Where a case will run past its target, the person who raised it is told in writing why and when to expect the next update, with updates continuing at least every 10 business days until the case closes.

Where an investigation will take longer, the reporter and the respondent are both told, in writing, why and when to expect the outcome. Complexity is a reason for delay; inattention is not.

Next steps:
- Contact People Operations if your case is not acknowledged within 4 business hours.
- Request a written update if investigation extends beyond initial timeline.

You are assigned to the Boston office and your manager Dana is Dana (Director, Engineering).

As a hybrid employee, you are required to work on site at least 3 days each week. The specific days are set by your team to ensure collaborative overlap, with most teams anchoring on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.

The requirement is measured as a rolling four-week average rather than week by week, so a single unusual week is never a compliance problem. Weeks containing company holidays, approved PTO or approved travel reduce the requirement proportionally.

Next steps:
- Confirm your team's specific onsite days with Dana.

You have 13.5 PTO days remaining.

PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance. A request of six or more consecutive business days requires 15 business days of advance notice. Notice is counted in business days between the day the request is submitted in MosaicOne and the first day of the requested absence, excluding both the submission day and any company holiday on your office calendar.

Your direct manager, Dana, approves PTO requests up to 5 consecutive business days with 5 business days' notice. Requests of 6 to 15 consecutive business days also go to Dana with 15 business days' notice. Requests longer than 15 consecutive business days require Dana's approval plus your director's approval, with 15 business days' notice.

Next steps:
- Plan your request timing based on length.
- Submit in MosaicOne for Dana's approval.

New hires become eligible for medical, dental and vision coverage 90 days after their hire date. Coverage begins on the day the waiting period ends.

The waiting period is not restarted by an internal transfer, a promotion, or a change from part-time to full-time status. It is restarted by a break in service of more than 26 weeks.
